answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed on proven fraud: a fake army must lock real funds per account, so creating thousands of sock puppets becomes ruinously expensive. Honest agents keep a growing reputation, like a meadow that spreads slowly from real roots, while a sudden ripple of brand-new accounts with no history triggers extra checks. Old credentials cannot be recycled as a relic of past trust — standing must be earned continuously through verified work, so attackers pay far more than they can ever gain.
